title: Your Family Member Needs Bail Money!
message: You receive a phone call from an unfamiliar international number. The caller claims that your cousin has been arrested while traveling in another country. They explain that your cousin is being held in jail and needs $2,500 immediately for bail. The caller says your cousin is scared and cannot contact anyone else. They demand payment through a money transfer service within the next hour and warn you not to tell other family members.

choices.text: Send the money immediately because your family member could be in danger.
choices.feedback: This is a family emergency impersonation scam. Scammers exploit fear and emotional attachment by pretending a loved one is in danger.

choices.text: Ask the caller for your cousin's personal information and send the money if they provide it.
choices.feedback: Scammers can often find or guess personal details, so this doesn't actually confirm the story is real.

choices.text: Contact your cousin or another trusted family member through a separate, verified communication method before taking action.
choices.feedback: Correct. Always independently verify through another channel before sending money.

choices.text: Send half the requested amount to show that you are willing to help.
choices.feedback: Sending any money without verifying the story still puts you at risk, scammers often come back asking for more.

warningSigns: Urgent demand for money within a short time frame
Caller discourages contacting other family members
Request for payment through a money transfer service
